advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider scanning loader-call keyword arguments (node.value.keywords) in _seam_loader_receivers, or document keyword-arg loader binding as accepted residual.
evidence: scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py:286: `named = any(` iterates only `for arg in node.value.args`
The module's own docstring warns 'under-binding would silently drop a real composition' (scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py:303), which is exactly the failure mode of the keyword-arg case
In-tree loader calls use positional args (reconcile_helpers.py:208 `_load("rebar_reconciler.git_adapter", "git_adapter.py")`), so no current false negative — this is a forward-looking gap
advisory.finding: _seam_loader_receivers only inspects positional args of the loader call (node.value.args); a dynamic module load that passes the git-adapter module path as a keyword argument (e.g. _load(name="...git_adapter", ...)) would not bind the receiver, silently under-binding and dropping a real R3 composition.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Qualify SEAM_INTERNAL_MODULES matching by package path (e.g. rebar_reconciler) rather than bare stem, or note the tree-wide stem match as accepted residual.
evidence: scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py:666: `seam = _NO_SEAM if rel.stem in SEAM_INTERNAL_MODULES else _seam_bindings(tree)`
SEAM_INTERNAL_MODULES = frozenset({"git_adapter", "_ref_lock", "_ref_lock_push"}) is matched by stem only, with no package/path qualification
The header documents this as an intentional per-file trust boundary (lines 62-73) but frames it as the three specific reconciler files, not 'any file with these names tree-wide'
advisory.finding: SEAM_INTERNAL_MODULES is matched against the bare `rel.stem`, so R3 is disabled for ANY file named git_adapter.py, _ref_lock.py, or _ref_lock_push.py anywhere under src/ or scripts/ — not only the reconciler write-seam package. A future unrelated module reusing one of those filenames would silently gain the seam's trust exemption.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an R3 test asserting `seam-composition` fires on a dotted-attribute receiver call, e.g. `pkg.git_adapter.add(d, "b.json")`.
evidence: scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py:469-476: `if isinstance(recv, ast.Name): name = recv.id  elif isinstance(recv, ast.Attribute): name = recv.attr ...`
Inline comment at scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py:466-467: "both ``git_adapter.add(…)`` and ``pkg.git_adapter.add(…)`` bind"

ABSENCE: the new R3 tests (test_r3_composed_add_commit_outside_seam_fires, test_r3_aliased_import_binding_fires, test_r3_from_imported_primitive_bare_name_fires, test_r3_dynamic_loader_binding_fires) use only Name-receiver, alias, from-import, or loader-Name forms; none writes a `pkg.git_adapter.add(...)` attribute-chain receiver.
advisory.finding: No test exercises the dotted-attribute receiver branch of R3 (`pkg.git_adapter.add(...)`), where the checker resolves the receiver by its trailing `.attr`. Both the header docstring and the inline comment explicitly cite this shape as supported, and the checker has a dedicated `isinstance(recv, ast.Attribute)` branch, but every new firing test uses either a bare `Name` receiver, an alias, a from-imported bare primitive, or a dynamic-loader Name. A regression removing/breaking the `ast.Attribute` receiver case (lines 471-472) would go undetected.
scenarios: A future refactor that drops or breaks the ast.Attribute receiver branch would still pass the test suite while silently ceasing to fire on `pkg.git_adapter.add(...)` compositions.
